item.title: Show HN: status: an emoji and your status, built with SvelteKit and Claude (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: I've been building something and it's out today: status. It's all about breaking the ice. Keeping in touch takes more than it should. A full post feels like a performance, a message out of the blue needs a reason and sometimes it means saying something in a group chat. So post an emoji and a few words, and your people can react, reply or message you for a natter. Everything has a status already: WhatsApp, Slack, Facebook. But there it sits on the side, something few people use in an app built for something else. I wanted it up front and centre. It's a SvelteKit and Svelte 5 web app with a Fastify and PostgreSQL api. The iPhone and Android apps are Capacitor shells around the live site. Sign in by email link or passkey, no passwords. No ads and no tracking. I built it with Claude. I write the requirements like ADRs, ai-dev-tasks turns them into a PRD and a task list, Claude Design draws it and Claude Code builds it with my own skills for design to code and for principles. My tip: pay attention. If you don't tell the robots how to behave and then check how they behaved, you'll get something you didn't ask for. How and why I built it: https://feedmypixel.com/status My skills: https://github.com/feedmypixel/principles iPhone: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6829789500 Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.status.me Have a play and let me know what you think. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50628286 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

item.title: Show HN: StoryPass - I turned my mom's paper game into a password generator (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: Hi HN, Cesar here, from Brazil. A lot of firsts here (post, app, launch), but bear with me, it's an honest try. TL;DR I built my 1st app, StoryPass. It makes passwords in line with NIST's latest guidelines, and it's available in the Mac App Store for $9.79 ($7.79 until Nov 30). You can learn more at usestorypass.com So every time I had to rotate my password at work, I got security chills (Summer%1 goes to Summer%2) and boredom at max. I wondered if there was a way to avoid it, and I was glad to learn that NIST, the US government agency that writes password guidelines, moved away from the dreaded 2003 rules (8 chars, upper/number and specials) in 2017, and in 2025 made a simple rule: 15 characters minimum. The guidelines changed because the human aspect was not really counted: our brain takes shortcuts around those rules, so a strong password became Password1! or even worse. So I built StoryPass, a password generator for macOS that uses a mini story - character, action, place - from a 15k-word dictionary to make long passwords that are easy to remember, like "Dad is dancing on the roof". It's a native app with a small one-time price, no ads, subscription or telemetry. If you'd like to try it, email support@usestorypass.com and I'll send you a promo code. I'd love to hear what you think about it. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50628249 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

item.title: Show HN: Knockbox - a drum machine that plays your beat like a drummer would (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: Hey HN. I've lost hours in the piano roll nudging kicks a few milliseconds late and snares a few early, trying to get a beat to feel like J Dilla's. As a dev i figured there was a better way so i built Knockbox. Concept is simple. One dial pulls the kick behind the beat while the snare pushes ahead of it, and each drum has its own dial for ghost notes. You also have a cool friend rocking with you on the desk who also listens to your drum patterns/loop and offers realtime ideas to get you that swing pocket you're after while still having creative freedom to override anything you want. You can also drop in a loop that auto-syncs to your beat tempo and the ability to export the MIDI, WAV or stems - or send a beat as a link that someone else can flip. It runs in the browser. nothing to install. Have fun Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50628247 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
